title: Throughput Recon — pulse map & quick heuristics
content:
Purpose:
Quick, disposable run to map short (10s–60s) surge behavior across two routing configs and three batch sizes. Want a light-weight pulse map to decide whether to tune routing policy or batch timeout first for incoming microbursts seen in product QA cluster. Not trying to be exhaustive — just capture signals and actionable heuristics.

Experiment summary (fast TL;DR):
- Workload: synthetic poisson pulse (10s on / 50s off) injected to a single model variant.
- Backends: routing-policy=A (aggressive multiplex) vs routing-policy=B (conservative lane isolation).
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 16.
- Client concurrency: fixed arrivals to target 120 QPS peak (measured at ingress).
- Measurement window: 12 minutes per run, repeated 3x per configuration.

Key metrics recorded: p50/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end), successful tokens/sec, KV cache hit fraction, batching utilization, GPU occupancy from infra traces.

Raw observations (most runs):
- Small batches (1): p50 ~ 12ms, p95 ~ 34ms, p99 ~ 110–220ms (heavy variance across pulses). Under routing-policy=A, p99 spikes were ~2x higher than policy=B at same batch=1.
- Medium batches (4): p50 ~ 18ms, p95 ~ 45ms, p99 ~ 140–260ms. Policy=A reduced p99 variance relative to policy=B at batch=4 — suggests multiplexing helps when there is some batching headroom.
- Large batches (16): p50 ~ 40ms, p95 ~ 120ms, p99 ~ 400–900ms. Both policies suffer; policy=A shows slightly better throughput but much worse tail latency.
- KV cache hit fraction during pulse ramp: drops by ~15–30% in first 8s of a pulse, recovers within 25–40s depending on inter-pulse spacing.

Example ASCII impulse trace (single run, policy=B, batch=4):
time(s) | qps(in) | p95(ms) | batch_util
0       | 5       | 40      | 0.18
5       | 120     | 46      | 0.72
10      | 118     | 52      | 0.78
20      | 8       | 37      | 0.22

Interpretation notes:
- Very small batches keep median latency low but suffer extreme p99 tails under aggressive multiplexing; likely interference from cross-tenant coalescing and longer scheduling queues on GPU kernels when many tiny contexts compete.
- Medium batching (4) seems a good compromise: modest median increase for much reduced p99 variance under policy=A.
- Large batches overwhelm priority lanes during the initial few seconds of a pulse (batch formation latency + preemption). If expected burst duration < 12s, large batches are net-negative for SLOs.
- KV cache warmup is non-trivial: repeated pulses with <30s spacing keep cache miss rate elevated. This explains higher token compute overhead on successive pulses.

Actionable heuristics to test next (small follow-ups):
1) Set batch_timeout to 6ms for batch_size=4 under policy=A and re-run pulses — hypothesize p95 improves without hurting throughput.
2) Try a soft cap on multiplexing concurrency (e.g., max-inflight-per-core) to alleviate tiny-request tail spikes observed with batch=1.
3) Run cache-priming shadow traffic (2–5% of peak) to see effect on p99 during pulses. If priming reduces p99 by >30%, consider prefill option for critical paths.
4) Add per-tenant admission control for pulses longer than 8s: route to variant with larger batch and bumped priority.

Open questions / uncertainties:
- Are the p99 spikes primarily scheduling jitter on CUDA kernels or coming from proxy-level queues? Need correlated low-level traces (kernel start/end timestamps).
- How sensitive are these observations to sequence length? Current runs used avg tokens=40; longer contexts may magnify batching costs.
- The infra traces we collected are noisy during ramp; we should add deterministic synthetic payloads to reduce variance.

Run metadata (for reproducibility):
- Model: open-llama-7b-quant (serving-variant v2024-11-30-quant)
